scenes.text: The Secrets API is committed to core in revision 64337, and will ship in WordPress 7.2. Here's how to use it.
scenes.caption: The Secrets API is committed to core in r64337, and will ship in WordPress 7.2. Here's how to use it.

scenes.text: Plugins keep API keys in options. Plain text. So a database dump, or a backup, leaks every one.
Store one with W P set secret: a name, and a value. You get back true, or a W P Error. Names look like plugin slug, slash, key name.
scenes.caption: Store one with wp_set_secret(): a name, and a value. You get back true, or a WP_Error. Names look like plugin-slug/key-name.

scenes.text: Reading has three outcomes. A W P Secret. Null, if there's no such secret. Or a W P Error, if it exists but can't be read. Call reveal for the value: a string, or a W P Error.
scenes.caption: Reading has three outcomes. A WP_Secret. null, if there's no such secret. Or a WP_Error, if it exists but can't be read. Call reveal() for the value: a string, or a WP_Error.

scenes.text: The value stays hidden. Echo it, log it, or encode it as JSON, and you get a placeholder. Serialize or clone it, and it throws. Only reveal returns the plaintext.
scenes.caption: The value stays hidden. Echo it, log it, or encode it as JSON, and you get a placeholder. Serialize or clone it, and it throws. Only reveal() returns the plaintext.

scenes.text: Got a key in an option already? Import it. The option stays untouched, and the secret is flagged for rotation, since it's lived in plain text.
Set a new value, and the old one becomes the previous version. Read it with W P Secret Version PREVIOUS while you switch over, then retire it.
scenes.caption: Set a new value, and the old one becomes the previous version. Read it with WP_Secret_Version::PREVIOUS while you switch over, then retire it.

scenes.text: Under the hood: libsodium, XChaCha20 Poly1305. Each value gets its own data key, wrapped by a master key from a root key, which your site key wraps. That site key comes from W P SECRETS KEY, or from the logged in key and salt. It never touches the database.
scenes.caption: Under the hood: libsodium, XChaCha20-Poly1305. Each value gets its own data key, wrapped by a master key from a root key, which your site key wraps. That site key comes from WP_SECRETS_KEY, or from LOGGED_IN_KEY and LOGGED_IN_SALT. It never touches the database.

scenes.text: Site Health checks that setup, and recommends a dedicated key.

On multisite, there are network twins. Two capabilities: manage secrets for administrators, manage network secrets for super admins. The functions themselves don't check capabilities. Do that at your own boundary.
scenes.caption: On multisite, there are network twins. Two capabilities: manage_secrets for administrators, manage_network_secrets for super admins. The functions themselves don't check capabilities. Do that at your own boundary.

scenes.text: Hosts get a drop-in. A secrets dot P H P in wp-content loads before must-use plugins. Set the provider, store or keyring, and implement the interface. Conformance tests for drop-in authors ship in core.
scenes.caption: Hosts get a drop-in. A secrets.php in wp-content loads before must-use plugins. Set the provider, store or keyring, and implement the interface. Conformance tests for drop-in authors ship in core.

scenes.text: If it breaks, every call returns a W P Error. It never falls back. The feature plugin's examples ran against AWS KMS, AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault and OpenBao.
scenes.caption: If it breaks, every call returns a WP_Error. It never falls back. The feature plugin's examples ran against AWS KMS, AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault and OpenBao.

scenes.text: For an audit trail, hook W P secret changed: name, action, user, timestamp, fingerprints. Never a value.
scenes.caption: For an audit trail, hook wp_secret_changed: name, action, user, timestamp, fingerprints. Never a value.

scenes.text: Committed in revision 64337, shipping in WordPress 7.2. Admin screen planned for 7.3. W P CLI lives in the feature plugin. Docs at secrets A P I dot dev. Trac 66187. Go lock something up.
